articles.title: Latent Bridge: Asking for Help Without Words
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-based model collaboration requires a large model to generate intermediate responses before a smaller model can use its guidance, adding large-model decoding cost to inference. We introduce POND (Prefill-Only, No-Decode), a method that uses a frozen large sender for prefill and a small receiver for all autoregressive decoding. A trainable bridge maps the sender's hidden states to additional attention keys and values, allowing the receiver to use these representations throughout generation. POND also supports periodic review, in which the sender processes the receiver's partial response and updates its guidance through additional prefill passes while preserving the receiver's existing KV cache. Across reasoning and coding benchmarks, POND improves receiver performance with senders from different model families. In particular, GLM-5.3 provides gains comparable to those of Qwen3.8-Max when paired with a Qwen receiver, supporting the effectiveness of representation transfer between independently trained model families. POND further demonstrates its ability to generalize across domains. When trained on math and coding tasks, it transfers directly to general knowledge tasks without additional domain-specific training. These results demonstrate that large frontier model prefill representations can improve small-model generation without requiring large-model autoregressive decoding.

articles.title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) for Tibetan is evaluated predominantly by character error rate (CER). Tibetan marks syllable boundaries but does not mark word boundaries, so a word error rate requires a segmenter. This study evaluates nine recognizer configurations on typeset, woodblock and two handwritten script styles, alone and in combination, and reports syllable- and word-level error rates, to our knowledge the first for Tibetan OCR. The configurations span CTC models, TrOCR encoder-decoders with and without post-training quantization, and a vision-language model, and each is scored under CER, the syllable error rate (SER) and three segmented word error rates (SWER). CER ranks systems largely as the higher-level rates do (Kendall $\tau \geq 0.833$), with one pair ordered oppositely. On the effect of joint training, CER and SER record significant changes of opposite sign in 7 of 64 comparisons. SER needs no segmenter and ranks systems as SWER does under two of the three segmenters ($\tau \geq 0.889$). The output of each configuration is also tagged for part of speech, annotated for named entities and machine translated, and each result is compared with that obtained on the reference text. As rough guidance, translation chrF of 60 is reached at SER of 0.047 or below and part-of-speech preservation of 0.8 at 0.078 or below, while no error rate separates the systems that reach entity preservation of 0.6 from those that do not.

articles.title: What You Post Is What You Symptom: Estimating Psychometric Networks from Social Media Discourse
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symptom networks in psychopathology are estimated almost exclusively from self-report questionnaires, restricting inference to whatever symptom set a given instrument covers. We introduce a framework for symptom-resolved network estimation directly from social media discourse and apply the framework to depression and eating disorders, with a third anorexia corpus as cross-dataset validation. To our knowledge, we are the first to estimate symptom-resolved psychometric networks from social media text, compare them to clinical co-endorsement networks, and replicate transdiagnostic linguistic markers across 3 independently recruited corpora spanning 2 disorders simultaneously. For depression, expression scores correlate with BDI-II totals at $\rho{=}0.434$, 20 of 21 items reach FDR significance, and split-half reliability is 0.935. The Network Comparison Test detects few edge differences between modalities (3-5\% of edges), while bridge symptoms diverge. For eating disorders, the item-level results are exploratory. Identified linguistic features replicate the same direction across all 3 corpora, and they cluster in three construct families.

articles.title: Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models often produce hallucinated answers, motivating selective prediction policies that abstain on uncertain queries. However, heuristic uncertainty thresholds alone do not provide statistical control of errors among accepted predictions. Linear Expectation Constraints (LEC) reduce selection-conditioned error rate (SCER) calibration to a nonpositive expected linear-loss constraint, but the associated loss is non-monotonic in the acceptance threshold. We construct an exact counterexample under i.i.d. sampling demonstrating that LEC's empirical threshold-selection rule can violate the population SCER target. To address this risk-transfer gap, we introduce Stability-Compensated Linear Expectation Control (SC-LEC), which uses the negative linear risk of a theoretical full-data reference to compensate for threshold-selection instability. For local expansion beyond a safe anchor, we derive two finite-sample certificates: a stability-based certificate exploiting rank crossings and a direct certificate using the structure of threshold expansion to reduce conservatism. With a valid population anchor margin, our certificate conditions ensure finite-sample marginal SCER control, and independent margin certification further provides a $1-\delta$ high-probability guarantee for this calibration-averaged control. Experiments on CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, and TriviaQA show useful retention gains beyond the same certified anchor, while revealing conservative behavior in small-margin regimes.

articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning a small typed decision model on one user's email labels did not clear the margin we pre-registered over a logistic regression trained on the same labels. In earlier work, about two hundred labels and a TF-IDF logistic regression had the highest point accuracy on this inbox, though not significantly above the best hosted model; we ask whether the same labels, given to a decision model, close the gap. A first registered study, on a generic 4B base with cross-validation and message type only, stayed below the baseline at every label budget (-1.8 to -7.3 points). The main study was registered before any fine-tuning run: a fixed test set of 135 emails never used for selection, LoRA adapters on the public Tev1-0.8B and Tev1-4B decision models, nested subsets of 50 to 587 labels, two seeds and five decision fields on a free T4 GPU. Four of its five hypotheses are refuted--two in the fine-tunes' favour--and one is confirmed for one model. On message type the 4B model misses the registered three-point margin at 400 labels (+2.6) and passes it with all 587 (+3.3); with all labels both models are above the baseline by +0.7 and +3.3 points, where one email is 0.74 points and a 95% interval is about 15 points wide, and the 4B model is clearly ahead in type macro-F1 (0.581 vs. 0.406). On the three action switches the baseline is ahead at every label budget for both models (0.931 vs. 0.904 and 0.899 mean accuracy with all labels), at under a millisecond per question against 306 and 1681 ms. The 0.8B type curve barely improves after 300 labels and then falls. The baseline never predicts the two rarest classes (7 offers and 8 spam in the training pool); the fine-tuned models find spam in some runs, not consistently across seeds

articles.title: Rubric-Based AES with LLM Ensembles: Scoring of Student Responses in Critical Online Reasoning Using Ensembles of LLMs
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grading student responses is costly and time-consuming. Moreover, human annotators are prone to bias, fatigue, and rater drift, which further limits grading reliability. Various methods have been employed to develop automated essay scoring (AES) systems to reduce these costs and address bias-related issues. These methods range from early text-feature-based systems to current machine-learning and transformer-based models. Specifically, large language models (LLMs) offer the potential to streamline the development of AES systems. However, they are subject to well-known limitations, such as hallucinations and prompt sensitivity. This creates a need to explore the potential of a mixed-methods approach that leverages the synergies among individual LLMs through ensemble formation. We evaluate the potential of ensembles of LLMs to match human-rater agreement when grading student responses in economics and medical education across 103 criteria. We use 631 German-language responses and corresponding human ratings by 2 to 5 annotators from a previously conducted assessment. We experiment with 523 rubric-based prompt configurations across 15 open-weight LLMs and assess their consistency with human raters using Krippendorff's alpha for inter-annotator agreement (IAA) and the Alternative Annotator Test (alt-test). Our results show that replacing one human rater with the best-performing LLM--prompt configuration maintains or improves IAA for 91 of the 103 criteria and that LLMs pass the alt-test for 90 criteria. Our findings suggest that current state-of-the-art LLMs can support AES of German responses in economics and medical education, reducing human workload and enabling faster processing, while validation against human ratings remai

articles.title: Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Researchers at MIT recently reported that GPT-6 Astra, a frontier large language model (LLM), can write the weights of small neural networks directly in a single reply, and can read the raw weights of small networks to say what they were trained to do. In a three-day sprint, we replicated and extended these results. Our four findings: (1) Writing weights reproduces. Astra's networks for the game Breakout scored 514, 550 and 307 (versus MIT's 517), and scored just as well on two modified versions of Breakout. Claude Opus 5.5 can also write working networks, but often runs out of output tokens. (2) What is new is translating programs into weights. Earlier models could write a good policy as code a generation before they could write network weights, and the networks the models write behave like compiled programs: two models independently decompiled Astra's Breakout network into Python matching its actions in all tested states. On classifying handwritten digits, Astra's networks scored 50% on average, below a simple classifier (82%). (3) Reading weights is mostly reading the input layer. Astra and Opus 5.5 identify which game a network plays almost perfectly, but on three new games we designed and trained ourselves, Astra recovered where things are on the board, while mostly missing how the game works. (4) Auditing from weights alone is possible but shallow. Without executing code, Astra picked out a small language model poisoned during training in 10 of 10 runs, one poisoned by extra training afterwards in 7 of 10, and a malicious adapter in 23 of 32 cases, but never identified the trigger or malicious behaviour. Open-weight models lag behind. From this early study, we conclude that LLMs can read and write small networks, but

articles.title: A Scalable Multi Task Learning Framework for Modeling Demographic Disagreements in Annotation Tasks
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Annotators from different demographic backgrounds often disagree in systematic ways due to varying lived experiences, cultural contexts, and their relationship to the content. When such disagreement occurs, one group's perspective may sometimes warrant prioritization because they hold an epistemically advantaged standpoint or bear greater stake in the outcome. For example, when assessing toxicity of posts on social media, it may be important to prioritize a targeted group's viewpoint. We propose a Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning (SAJ-MTL) framework to jointly model demographic disagreement both across- and within- annotator groups. The model uses conditional gradient routing to handle sparsity induced by group-conditional labeling, and parameterization supports customized weighting of groups in different task settings. SAJ-MTL improves group-level performance in toxicity detection through better context-aware understanding of demographic-sensitive content. Only annotator group-membership information is required, which is more practical than existing methods requiring more privacy-invasive individual-level annotator details. Our scalable architecture is also computationally efficient to support large-scale deployment.

articles.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A useful memory need not resemble the question it helps answer. Jetriever ranks each stored memory by Jev's decision score for its usefulness to the current question, replacing similarity search with full-pool utility scoring. On InMind's 125 indirect-query tasks, it places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of cases; matched BM25 and MiniLM controls reach 1.6% and 0.0% when indexing user turns. A 20-question comparison separates finding evidence from ranking it: Jev and Qwen3.5 9B each find 90% of gold exchanges by rank 50, while Laya finds 30%; at rank one, Jev reaches 85% and Qwen3.5 9B 40%. On a dimension-proportional random sample of 60 MemoryAgentBench questions, Jetriever's four-dimension score is 55.4%, against 44.3% for ReFind on the same questions. Jev retrieval costs USD 0.00834 per InMind question and USD 0.03103 per MAB question on average. These results show the value of world knowledge, scores that rank decisive memories first, and affordable full-pool scoring.

articles.title: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings is a standard measure of whether online discourse is converging under generative AI. When the embeddings are mean-pooled outputs of an encoder never trained for sentence similarity, this measure mostly tracks text length. In 6.06 million Reddit comments, an uncentered DeBERTa-v3 measure had suggested that only conservative discourse broke toward homogeneity after late 2022. Truncating the same comments from 10 to 150 words raises their mean cosine by eight times the reported break. A placebo that swaps every comment for a random one of equal length reproduces 81% of the asymmetry, and a fixed-content simulation reproduces 78%. The leading principal direction carries 99.9% of raw DeBERTa homogeneity, and once length is handled the asymmetry disappears under every encoder. On 575,000 Stack Exchange answers the measure reports a post-ChatGPT homogenization of technical sites that the placebo fully reproduces, although answers grew longer. A census of 31 studies locates the risk where anisotropic encoders meet time-series or length-unequal designs. A reverse control on a well-known experiment shows that centering with renormalization can reverse a genuine effect. I propose a low-cost diagnostic protocol. Corrected measures show that the two political camps converged between 2019 and 2022 and stopped converging before ChatGPT. Cross-camp replies engage their targets more closely than same-camp replies.

articles.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings. Although sentiment analysis is a common task in this area, affective meaning in social media discourse is often conveyed through culturally situated and pragmatically indirect cues that are not well captured by label-centric evaluation alone. In this paper, we evaluate the robustness of LLMs for sentiment analysis of Spanish political discourse from social media, with emphasis on culturally situated affective interpretation. We introduce a diagnostic protocol that combines three independent human annotation views into Gold and Ambiguous subsets, and extends the corpus with a Synthetic subset built from sentiment-flipped counterfactuals selected through model-conditioned perplexity and LLM-as-a-judge criteria. Using this framework, we compare proprietary and open-weight models under zero-shot and few-shot prompting, focusing on predictive robustness across human agreement conditions and counterfactual shift. Our results show that annotation ambiguity and counterfactual perturbation reveal failure modes that conventional evaluation on the original corpus tends to obscure. GPT-4.1-mini remains the most stable among the evaluated models, whereas the two smaller open-weight models degrade more markedly under synthetic perturbations, and few-shot prompting provides only limited gains. Overall, the paper contributes a reproducible protocol for robustness-oriented evaluation in political sentiment analysis, an empirical characterization of model behavior under ambiguity and sentiment-flipped counterfactuals, and a publicly available

articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.21586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026. We first apply PERC, short for Preprocessing (P), Embedding (E), Dimensionality Reduction (R) and Clustering (C). We employ GPT-6 Luna to classify job description passages into Team context, Role task and Qualifications. We then create combinations of these sections and examine whether embedding and clustering the segmented passages produce meaningful semantic clusters about different job roles. We use Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to rank observed differences between embedding distributions and employ a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to extract features from layer-19 representations of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Lastly, we employ GPT-6 Luna to come up with hypotheses about job roles' feature patterns, and GPT-6.1 Terra to investigate whether those patterns exist in held-out job descriptions from unseen companies. Some example findings include Data Scientist advertisements placing more emphasis on machine learning model development, Data Analyst advertisements on reporting business performance, and Machine Learning Engineer advertisements on applying developed models in real-world settings. We also observe differences in the applications described by Data Analyst and Business Analyst advertisements across selected months, although our dataset's scale and uneven coverage limit their interpretation. articles.title: Using the Tsetlin Machine to Learn Human-Interpretable Rules for High-Accuracy Text Categorization with Medical Applications
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:1809.04547v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical applications challenge today's text categorization techniques by demanding both high accuracy and ease-of-interpretation. Although deep learning has provided a leap ahead in accuracy, this leap comes at the sacrifice of interpretability. To address this accuracy-interpretability challenge, we here introduce, for the first time, a text categorization approach that leverages the recently introduced Tsetlin Machine. In all brevity, we represent the terms of a text as propositional variables. From these, we capture categories using simple propositional formulae, such as: if "rash" and "reaction" and "penicillin" then Allergy. The Tsetlin Machine learns these formulae from a labelled text, utilizing conjunctive clauses to represent the particular facets of each category. Indeed, even the absence of terms (negated features) can be used for categorization purposes. Our empirical comparison with Na\"ive Bayes, decision trees, linear support vector machines (SVMs), random forest, long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks, and other techniques, is quite conclusive. The Tsetlin Machine either performs on par with or outperforms all of the evaluated methods on both the 20 Newsgroups and IMDb datasets, as well as on a non-public clinical dataset. On average, the Tsetlin Machine delivers the best recall and precision scores across the datasets. Finally, our GPU implementation of the Tsetlin Machine executes 5 to 15 times faster than the CPU implementation, depending on the dataset. We thus believe that our novel approach can have a significant impact on a wide range of text analysis applications, forming a promising starting point for deeper natural language understanding with the Tsetlin Machine.

articles.title: The Sharpness Disparity Principle in Transformers for Accelerating Language Model Pre-Training
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2502.19002v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transformers consist of diverse building blocks, such as embedding layers, normalization layers, self-attention mechanisms, and point-wise feedforward networks. Thus, understanding the differences and interactions among these blocks is important. In this paper, we uncover a clear Sharpness Disparity across these blocks, which emerges early in training and intriguingly persists throughout the training process. Motivated by this finding, we propose Blockwise Learning Rate (LR), a strategy that tailors the LR to each block's sharpness, accelerating large language model (LLM) pre-training. By integrating Blockwise LR into AdamW, we consistently achieve lower terminal loss and nearly $2\times$ speedup compared to vanilla AdamW. We demonstrate this acceleration across GPT-2 and LLaMA, with model sizes ranging from 0.12B to 2B and datasets of OpenWebText, MiniPile, and C4. Finally, we incorporate Blockwise LR into Adam-mini (Zhang et al., 2024), a recently proposed memory-efficient variant of Adam, achieving a combined $2\times$ speedup and $2\times$ memory saving. These results underscore the potential of exploiting the sharpness disparity to improve LLM training.

articles.title: Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.19123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways manage tool catalogs for language model agents using two primary paradigms: code mode where agents write scripts against tool stubs and decision layers which are cheap routers that preselect tool subsets. Using a controlled harness across 12 servers, up to 1,958 distractor tools, and three open-weight agents including Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, we present a preregistered evaluation on a sealed test split to determine when each approach succeeds. Code mode substantially outperforms plain MCP, cutting token usage by 70 to 90 percent while significantly boosting utility. Declaring return-shape hints in code mode stubs is a first-order variable, swinging success by up to 39.5 points for lower-performing agents, an effect larger than adding a router. The central hypothesis that a decision layer in front of code mode beats code mode alone is not confirmed, showing minor, statistically non-significant improvements for weaker agents and a slight cost for the strongest. We publicly release our harness, a finetuned 4B tool selection model, and all evaluation traces to support robust community experimentation on local AI privacy and agent architectures.

articles.title: Auditory-Feedback-Conditioned Flow TTS for Implicit Lombard Adaptation
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.19260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional text-to-speech (TTS) systems can lose intelligibility in noise environments because they cannot adapt to environmental changes. However, humans tend to increase their vocal efforts in noisy environments, a phenomenon known as the Lombard effect. Building on an auditory-feedback Lombard TTS, we investigate whether a pretrained Flow-based TTS can learn acoustic adaptation directly from auditory feedback without explicit prosodic control. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) feedback and automatic speech recognition (ASR) feedback are extracted from the noise-corrupted waveforms and injected into the Flow-matching condition for utterance refinement and causal block-level updates. We assess feedback benefits across prompting and noise conditions using plain/Lombard prompting, prompt-switching controls, and paired-finetuning. Experiments show that while finetuning provides strong robustness under in-domain conditions, auditory feedback yields additional cue-dependent benefits that generalize to unseen noise. Moreover, stronger power/F0 tracking alone does not guarantee better speech intelligibility or quality.

articles.title: Can AI Judge You? An Empirical Audit of Deployment Readiness in LLM-assisted Hiring Systems
articles.feed_excerpt: arXiv:2611.20140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Delegating resume screening to large language models (LLMs) requires organizations to establish whether they can distinguish candidates by relevant qualifications while allowing only authorized users to change screening rules or approve exceptions. To this end, we develop a system architecture that separates candidate evidence, evaluation, permission controls, and assessment record, and empirically examine two complementary dimensions of its deployment readiness. First, we assess its operational readiness on four LLMs using a controlled experiment on 210 resumes across 14 job roles and six decision interfaces. Second, we assess its compliance readiness by testing how it handles unauthorized user requests and instructions embedded in resumes. We find that operational performance depends on the choice of evaluation interface: scalar scores generally distinguish qualification changes better than simple pass/fail judgments, while comparative judgments are sensitive to presentation order. Explicit permission rules and separation of resume content from instructions reduce unauthorized compliance, to a varying degree of effectiveness across LLMs and usage contexts. Finally, we find that LLM evaluators often diverge between their decisions and offered justifications. Going beyond simply evaluating LLMs for hiring tasks, our framework supports an audit of a fully configured resume evaluation system to enable its deployment decision.

articles.feed_excerpt: 深圳廣電集團聯同北京廣播電視台、上海廣播電視台推出《APEC「中國年」100小時全媒體大直播》節目。 報道指，深圳多間企業在APEC會議周期間，開展靈活辦公。哈工鵬澤 (深圳) 機器人技術有限公司工作人員姚佩彤表示，APEC周期間，公司遵循政府倡導，安排員工休年假、居家辦工或錯峰出行，平常有15人上班，今日只有4人返回辦公室工作。 美團外賣深圳負責人牛得旭說，美團外賣應用程式配合有關部門，推出中英雙語美食地圖，讓境內外來賓體驗到深圳的各類美食。 美團配送區域騎手保障經理袁敏說，在本周一至五推出10項保障措施，對深圳全市騎手超時訂單實行免責，部分重點區域如果出現特殊情況和路況問題，導致取消訂單，亦給予免責，希望減輕騎手的壓力，並根據騎手的跑單經驗和接單意願，將騎手最高接單量調低 2至3單，希望保障外賣騎手收入並確保交通安全。 中山大學國際關係學院教授孫興傑表示，中國的確定性來自於經濟總量政策的一貫性和發展前景的可預期性，是不確定世界當中最大的確定性，在新一輪的產業革命，中國已處於前沿，相信到深圳的各國領導人和工商界人士會有更切身體會。 孫興傑認為，APEC中國年在現時的國際關係中，具有顯著意義，亞太地區是全球穩定和發展的地區，中國是亞太地區的穩定器和壓艙石，提出順應亞太地區發展潮流和需要的務實措施，又形容國家十五五規劃的政策，不僅是中國的、也是亞太地區的。 編輯：譚佩貞

articles.title: APEC领导人会议周期间将继续围绕贸易议题寻求“最大公约数”
articles.feed_excerpt: 今天(17日)上午，2026年APEC领导人会议周新闻中心举办第五场吹风会，2026年APEC高官会主席陈旭介绍，APEC因应经济全球化而生，贸易自由化和便利化一直是APEC合作的核心议题。作为今年APEC东道主，中方将开放作为APEC“中国年”三大优先领域之一，目的就是要推动各方坚持开放的区域主义和真正的多边合作，坚定维护全球多边贸易体系，提升区域一体化水平，维护良好贸易投资环境，为区域和世界经济注入更多稳定性和确定性。在今年5月举行的APEC贸易部长会上，各方普遍认可世贸组织对促进全球贸易的关键作用，重申对亚太自贸区长期愿景的坚定支持，呼吁在能力建设、经验分享、技术合作等方面加大投入。亚太工商界就支持亚太自贸区建设发表了联合声明，充分体现了各方对于推进亚太自贸区的广泛共识和强烈愿望。APEC领导人会议周期间，各方将继续围绕贸易议题进行深入讨论，积极寻求“最大公约数”，中方期待在本次APEC领导人非正式会议上达成更多贸易领域务实成果，为区域经济一体化提供更大助力。

articles.title: 李家超：香港通過強化「四中心、一高地」定位 對接國家發展戰略
articles.feed_excerpt: 行政長官李家超表示，香港第一個五年規劃提出鞏固提升香港國際金融、航運、貿易中心地位，建設國際創新科技中心，打造國際高端人才集聚高地，通過強化「四中心、一高地」的定位，主動對接國家發展戰略。特區政府會積極落實這份規劃藍圖，一方面鞏固提升自身優勢，另一方面培育新動能，讓香港在世界變局中站得更穩、走得更遠。 李家超在一個論壇視像致辭表示，當前世界百年變局加速演進，地緣政治複雜多變。在變局中，香港更要發揮好自身優勢。香港是全球三大金融中心之一，在最自由經濟體排名多年保持世界第一，世界競爭力排名位居全球第二，具備充分的國際優勢，支持未來發展再創高峰。 他表示，面對全球貿易秩序重塑，內地企業積極出海，開拓市場。特區政府會更主動把國際資金「引進來」，助力企業「走出去」。本港已成立內地企業出海專班，協助企業以香港作為跳板拓展全球市場。本港亦正全速發展北部都會區，吸引龍頭企業和全球人才匯聚，當局將會加快河套香港園區建設，推動產學研協同轉化，促進科研成果更快落地和產業化，帶動產業升級。同時會培育新興創科產業，積極對接「人工智能+」等國家戰略，為傳統產業賦能，開拓新增長點，把握國家加快發展新質生產力的時代機遇。 他深信只要堅定發揮「一國兩制」優勢，抓緊國家發展機遇，守正創新，香港定能在新形勢下，續創高峰。 編輯：譚佩貞
articles.verification: 来源报道 · 尚未交叉核验

articles.title: 深圳APEC｜陳旭稱人工智能問題須共同研究 凝聚廣泛國際共識
articles.feed_excerpt: 2026年APEC高官會主席陳旭表示，粵港澳大灣區是中國高水平對外開放的窗口，亦是連接世界經濟往來一個重要樞紐，在中國經濟發展和對外開放中，發揮重要作用。他認為粵港澳大灣區的成功典範，回答了亞太合作應當向何處去的時代質問。 他說，大灣區的建設越來越重要，以深圳為例，由不為人知的小漁村，變成為現代化的國際大都市，是中國奉行互利共贏，開放戰略的一個生動體現。現時深圳已經被譽為中國的矽谷和中國南方科技中心，是粵港澳大灣區主要城市之一，集合十五五規劃中的好多重點，是中國式現代化成就的一個重要象徵，相信這些不同程度與APEC的宗旨理念和合作方向相契合、相呼應。 他又說，一直主張人工智能應該是普惠、向善，將來要造福全人類，不應當成為某一個群體和某一個國家獨有的東西。人工智能相關的問題，需要大家共同研究、共同商議，才能凝聚廣泛的國際共識，認為APEC經濟體在數字經濟和人工智能等新興科技議題上，有廣泛的共識和堅實的合作基礎。 編輯：譚佩貞

articles.title: The Fantasticks review – gay reimagining of musical is a heartwarming delight
articles.feed_excerpt: Hayes theater, New York City The world’s longest running musical is brought to Broadway for the first time in a joyful new version If you, like no doubt millions of tenderhearts the world over, are mourning the end of the Netflix series Heartstopper – a sweet and whimsical chronicling of two teenage boys in love – then all you need to do is book a trip to New York City and secure a ticket to the new production of The Fantasticks , the beloved musical now receiving its first-ever Broadway run. The show, from writers Tom Jones (not the one you’re thinking of) and Harvey Schmidt, ran for more than 40 years off-Broadway, the whole time telling the story of young lovers, Matt and Luisa, secretly pushed toward one another by their meddling parents. On Broadway, though, it has become the courtship of Matt (Maxim Chlumecky) and Lewis (Nathan Levy), two lads springy of hair and bouncy of step as they bound toward the rest of their lives together. The parents, fathers in the original production, have been switched to mothers, flower gardener Mildred (Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer) and avid vegetable grower Bessie (Ruthie Ann Miles), perhaps to add a few more female voices to this enduringly winsome (though some might say cloying) chamber piece. Those modern tweaks might be necessary, as so much of The Fantasticks is firmly rooted in the tones, tempos and tastes of another era. The musical first premiered in 1960, and its quaint attitudes about love and marriage, about childhood and what comes after it have otherwise not been meddled with in director-choreographer Christopher Gattelli’s lively and wistful new production. articles.title: 深圳APEC｜陳旭：各方共同努力下會議一定會取得圓滿成功
articles.feed_excerpt: 在深圳，APEC領導人會議周新聞中心舉辦第五場吹風會。 2026年APEC高官會主席陳旭表示，APEC領導人非正式會議即將舉行，會議的成果文件磋商工作已經啟動，正錨定亞太共同體建設這一個核心目標，在已經取得眾多務實合作成果的基礎上，進一步凝聚共識，主要體現在推動發表一份富有雄心的領導人成果文件，規劃各方建設亞太共同體的共識和要採取的行動，亦積極推動在貿易聯通和創新領域打造務實的成果，為APEC在相關領域的合作注入新的動力。 他說，相信在各方共同努力下，今次領導人非正式會議一定會取得圓滿成功。 他又提到，中國第三次擔任APEC東道主，近一年以來圍繞建設亞太共同體，促進共同繁榮的主題和開放，創新合作的3大優先領域，積極開展籌備工作，至今在全國16個城市舉辦300多場會議和活動，各個經濟體的代表們開展廣泛深入討論，就共同關注的問題和合作領域達成豐富的共識。 編輯：譚佩貞

articles.title: 深圳APEC｜工商領導人峰會 習近平明天上午將發表主旨演講
articles.feed_excerpt: 2026年亞太經合組織工商領導人峰會一連兩日在深圳前海舉行，主題為「共促繁榮、共贏未來」。 峰會主席、中國貿促會會長任鴻斌致歡迎辭時表示，國家主席習近平明天上午將出席峰會開幕式，並發表主旨演講。澳洲、加拿大、智利、中國香港、印尼、韓國、馬來西亞、俄羅斯等11名APEC經濟體領導人，亦將出席峰會並發表演講、致辭或參與專題研討。 任鴻斌又說，今屆峰會聚焦開放、創新、合作三大優先領域，APEC全部21個經濟體和英國、法國、德國等13個域外經濟體，2000多名政商界代表參與。今日將圍繞互聯互通、人工智能、亞太可持續發展、亞太自貿區建設、數字經濟、粵港澳大灣區與亞太發展機遇等議題展開研討。今次峰會集亞太工商界全年磋商研討對話交流之大成，將形成並發布2026年亞太經合組織工商領導人峰會深圳倡議，也是工商峰會創辦30年來，首次以倡議形式發布成果文件。 任鴻斌指出，長期以來，工商界積極支持、參與和促進亞太合作與發展，推動亞太實現大發展、大繁榮、大融通，使亞太成為全球經濟最具活力的地區和主要的增長引擎。今年中國「十五五」規劃實現良好開局，中國經濟持續向新、向優、向好，新質生產力加快發展，中國機遇2.0正不斷為各國工商界帶來市場紅利、改革紅利、開放紅利和創新紅利。今次各人到深圳出席峰會，都會感受到與中國同行就是與機遇同行，相信中國就是相信未來。 任鴻斌期望各方在對話研討中激發思想，凝聚廣泛共識，在溝通交流中達成合作，匯聚強大合力，在亞太經貿合作進程中，再次留下中國印記，為共建亞太共同體、共促全球增長繁榮作出新的更大貢獻。 編輯：譚佩貞
